title: Sections formula for the etale-to-pro-etale inverse image
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, with small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the universes and skeletons fixed there. Let $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}	o X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. For a weakly etale $X$-scheme $f:Y	o X$ that is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, let $f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets on the small etale sites, defined by the adjunction and sheafified presheaf construction in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and let $\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},G)=G(Y)$ denote sections at the identity etale object. The presheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with values
$$A_X(F)(Y)=\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$$
and restriction along $g:Z	o Y$ given by etale section pullback followed by the canonical composition identification $g_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F\cong(fg)_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F$ is a sheaf. There is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of sets $
u_X^*F\cong A_X(F)$, natural in $F$. For $U	o X$ etale, its component identifies the comparison adjunction unit $F(U)	o(
u_X^*F)(U)$ with the usual identification $F(U)\cong\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},F|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}})$.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, label lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale (statement and adjunction construction); comparison morphism in Tag 099R, label section-comparison

proof.text: For $g:Z\to Y$ define $r_g$ on $A_X(F)(Y)$ by the inverse-image unit on global sections followed by $c_{f,g,F}$. The unit formula (1) and associativity (2) give $r_h r_g=r_{gh}$: both send a section to its twice-pulled-back section and then use the equal composition comparisons. For an identity morphism the presheaf inverse-image formula is the original presheaf: at $V$ the pair $(V,\mathrm{id})$ is initial in the category of pairs and hence terminal in its opposite. Sheafification leaves this sheaf unchanged by its universal property. Thus $r_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. Naturality (0) in a sheaf morphism makes $F\mapsto A_X(F)$ a functor of presheaves.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, presheaf rule and its functoriality; Sites Tag 03CB for composition

proof.text: Let $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}$ be a pro-etale covering. It is fpqc by the site definition. Apply fpqc descent to the scheme $Y$ and the set sheaf $f^{-1}F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. It gives the equalizer of its sections over $Y$, the $Y_i$, and $Y_i\times_Y Y_j$. The composition-unit comparisons identify these terms, and both arrows, with $A_X(F)(Y)$, $A_X(F)(Y_i)$ and $A_X(F)(Y_i\times_Y Y_j)$ and the restrictions from Step 1. Consequently $A_X(F)$ is a sheaf, including the empty cover of the empty object. The argument requires neither quasi-compactness nor quasi-separatedness of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, first proof paragraph; Tag 098A lemma-recognize-proetale-covering; Etale Cohomology Tag 09XN lemma-describe-pullback

proof.text: For an etale $e:U\to X$, its inverse image on sets is restriction, as follows directly from the given presheaf construction. For $V\to U$ etale, the composite $V\to X$ is etale, and a pair $(W,\varphi:V\to U\times_X W)$ is equivalently an $X$-map $V\to W$. The pair $(V,V\to U\times_X V)$ is initial in this category, so the colimit over its opposite is $F(V)$ by restriction along $V\to W$. These identifications are natural in $V$ and $F$. Restriction $V\mapsto F(V\to X)$ is a sheaf because an etale cover over $U$ is an etale cover of the same object over $X$. The sheafification universal property therefore gives $e^{-1}F\cong F|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$. Under it the unit on $W$ is restriction along $U\times_X W\to W$. Evaluating at $V=U$ gives a natural bijection $j_{F,U}:F(U)\to A_X(F)(U)$, explicitly sending $s$ first to its inverse-image unit section $e^*s$ on $U\times_XU$ and then restricting along the diagonal $U\to U\times_XU$. These bijections form $j_F:F\cong\nu_{X,*}A_X(F)$ by the unit/composition formulas.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, paragraph F = epsilon_* a(F); detail of etale restriction via the inverse-image construction

proof.text: Given a pro-etale sheaf $G$ and $\alpha:F\to\nu_{X,*}G$, define $G_Y(V\to Y)=G(V\to X)$ for $f:Y\to X$ weakly etale. This is well defined: the comparison inclusion over $Y$ makes an etale $V\to Y$ weakly etale, and weakly etale composition makes $V\to X$ an object. The fpqc-finer-than-etale lemma makes every etale covering family over $Y$ fpqc; its arrows are weakly etale by the comparison inclusion over $Y$. Hence it is a pro-etale covering of the same object over $X$ by the pro-etale site definition, and the sheaf equalizer for $G$ makes $G_Y$ an etale sheaf. Define $b_Y:F\to f_*G_Y$ on $U\to X$ as $\alpha_U$ followed by restriction $G(U)\to G(Y\times_XU)$. All these objects exist by etale base change and weakly etale composition. Restriction functoriality makes $b_Y$ a morphism of sheaves. The sets inverse-image adjunction gives its unique transpose $t_Y:f^{-1}F\to G_Y$. Put $\beta_Y=\Gamma(Y,t_Y):A_X(F)(Y)\to G(Y)$.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, construction of a(epsilon_*G) -> G, with alpha inserted before restriction

proof.text: The maps $\beta_Y$ are natural for every $X$-map $g:Z\to Y$, without assuming $g$ etale. Restriction defines $d_g:G_Y\to g_*G_Z$, with component $G(V)\to G(Z\times_YV)$ at $V\to Y$; let $\rho_g:g^{-1}G_Y\to G_Z$ be its transpose. Compare $a=\rho_g\circ g^{-1}(t_Y)$ and $b=t_Z\circ c_{f,g,F}$, both from $g^{-1}f^{-1}F$ to $G_Z$. Take their transposes successively under $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ and $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. At $U\to X$ these are maps $F(U)\to G(Z\times_XU)$: the transpose of $a$ sends $s$ first to $\alpha_U(s)|_{Y\times_XU}$ and then restricts to $Z\times_XU$, by the defining equations for $t_Y$ and $\rho_g$; the transpose of $b$ sends $s$ directly to $\alpha_U(s)|_{Z\times_XU}$, by the composition-unit formula (1) and the defining equation for $t_Z$. Restriction functoriality makes these values equal for every $U,s$, so injectivity of the two adjunction bijections gives $a=b$. Evaluate on the $g$-pullback of a section of $f^{-1}F$ over $Y$. The defining equation for $\rho_g$ identifies the left value with $G(g)\beta_Y$, and the right value is $\beta_Zr_g$. Thus $\beta$ is a sheaf morphism. For $\psi:F'\to F$, the defining maps satisfy $b_Y(\alpha\psi)=b_Y(\alpha)\psi$; for $\chi:G\to G'$, they satisfy $b_Y((\nu_*\chi)\alpha)=f_*(\chi|_{Y_{\mathrm{et}}})b_Y(\alpha)$. Naturality of the inverse-image adjunction and evaluation gives naturality of $\beta$ in both variables.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, putting the transposes together for all f; omitted verification supplied by taking the two successive adjunction transposes

proof.text: Conversely, a sheaf morphism $\beta:A_X(F)\to G$ gives $\alpha=\nu_{X,*}(\beta)j_F$. Starting with $\alpha$ and constructing $\beta$, on etale $U$ and $s\in F(U)$ the formula for $t_U$ sends the unit section on $U\times_XU$ to $\alpha_U(s)$ restricted there; pulling back along the diagonal sends it to $\alpha_U(s)$ itself. Thus the reconstructed $\alpha$ equals the original. For the other composite, start with $\beta$. Fix $Y$ and any etale $V\to Y$. Step 3 over $Y$ identifies $(V\to Y)^{-1}f^{-1}F$ with the restriction of $f^{-1}F$ to $V$. Its sections are $A_X(F)(V)$ by the composition comparison. Hence the components $\beta_V$ define a sheaf morphism $f^{-1}F\to G_Y$. On a unit section coming from $s\in F(U)$ at $Y\times_X U$, naturality of $\beta$ for $Y\times_XU\to U$ identifies its value with $\alpha_U(s)$ restricted to $Y\times_XU$. It therefore has transpose $b_Y$, so adjunction uniqueness makes it $t_Y$. At $V=Y$ this says the reconstructed $\beta_Y$ is the original. We have obtained mutually inverse, natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(A_X(F),G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,\nu_{X,*}G)$ with unit $j_F$.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, final proof paragraph: full verification of the two mutually inverse Hom maps

proof.text:
The comparison definition gives another left adjoint $
u_X^*$ to the same restriction functor. The Hom bijection of Step 6 sends the comparison unit $\eta_F:F	o
u_{X,*}
u_X^*F$ to $q_F:A_X(F)	o
u_X^*F$. The comparison adjunction sends $j_F$ to $p_F:
u_X^*F	o A_X(F)$. By the defining equations, $
u_{X,*}(p_F)\eta_F=j_F$ and $
u_{X,*}(q_F)j_F=\eta_F$. Therefore $p_Fq_F$ corresponds under Step 6 to $j_F$, just as $\mathrm{id}_{A_X(F)}$ does, and $q_Fp_F$ corresponds under the comparison adjunction to $\eta_F$, just as $\mathrm{id}_{
u_X^*F}$ does. Injectivity of the two Hom bijections gives both inverse identities. Naturality of the bijections makes $p_F$ natural in $F$. At an etale $U$, its defining equation sends the comparison unit to $j_{F,U}$, exactly the identification in Step 3. This proves every clause, with the canonical isomorphism oriented $
u_X^*F\cong A_X(F)$.
